title: Policy evaluation, policy iteration, and value iteration
brief: Compute values by repeated Bellman sweeps, find optimal policies two ways, and watch the error shrink by a factor of gamma every sweep.
hints: A synchronous sweep computes the whole new vector from the old one: new = r_pi + gamma * P_pi @ v. Don't overwrite v entry by entry during a sweep.
greedy_policy: q = rlenvs.q_from_v(mdp, v), then put a 1 at q.argmax(axis=1) in each row. np.argmax already picks the lowest index among ties.
value_iteration's history starts with V_0 and gains one row per sweep, including the last one, so np.array(history) has shape (sweeps + 1, S).
sweeps_needed solves gamma^k * initial_error <= eps for k: math.ceil(math.log(eps / initial_error) / math.log(gamma)). Return 0 when the initial error is already small enough.
In policy_iteration, compare whole policies with np.array_equal(new_pi, pi) to decide when to stop.
